from.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison before the inverse limit: Infinity-categorical monadicity and the augmented counit bar resolution. Supporting foundation: Free coherent monad modules and their augmented free resolution. Supporting lemma: Underlying equivalences and operadic colimits of coherent modules. Supporting step: Coherent modules as inert-preserving simplicial sections.

title: Coherent modules as inert-preserving simplicial sections
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and sufficiently large universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], monoidal infinity-categories of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and inner and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $\mathcal V$ be monoidal, $\mathcal M$ coherently left-tensored over $\mathcal V$, and $B$ an associative algebra in $\mathcal V$; these structures include all higher associativity and unit compatibilities, with the operadic encoding of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. Write $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ for objects of $\mathcal M$ with coherent unital associative $B$-action, retaining action-preserving maps and all higher simplices, and $U$ for the underlying-object functor. There is a categorical fibration
$$q_B:X_B\longrightarrow N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$$
with the following properties. Categorical fibration means inner fibration with lifting of equivalence edges with specified source. It is locally cocartesian: pulling it back along any edge $\Delta^1\to N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ gives a cocartesian fibration. Its fiber at $[n]$ is equivalent to $\mathcal M$. If $\beta:[n]\to[m]$ is opposite to $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ in $\Delta$, its local transport, under these fiber identifications, is
$$\beta_!(x)\simeq B^{\otimes(n-\alpha(m))}\otimes x,$$
where the zeroth power acts as the identity via the unit constraint. For $x\in(X_B)_{[n]}$ and $y\in(X_B)_{[m]}$, the space of arrows over $\beta$ is naturally $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(\beta_!x,y)$; locally cocartesian arrows correspond to equivalences in this description.

Let $\Gamma(q_B)=\operatorname{Fun}_{N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})}(N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}),X_B)$ denote coherent sections and transformations whose image in the base is the identity transformation, with their higher simplices over the identity. Let $I$ consist of the arrows opposite to interval inclusions $\alpha:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$ with $\alpha(m)=n$. Then there is an equivalence
$$\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)\simeq\Gamma_I(q_B)\subseteq\Gamma(q_B),$$
where $\Gamma_I(q_B)$ is the full subcategory of sections carrying every edge of $I$ to a locally cocartesian edge. Under this equivalence evaluation at every $[n]$, followed by the fiber equivalence with $\mathcal M$, is naturally equivalent to $U$. These equivalences are supplied by the section edges opposite to $[0]\to[n]$, $0\mapsto n$. No colimit, limit or presentability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Corollary 4.2.2.16, Notation 4.2.2.17, Remarks 4.2.2.18-19, Lemma 4.2.2.20 and Remark 4.2.2.21 and condition (2') in Remark 4.2.2.19, printed pp. 518-519. Condition (2') there asks the inert edges with alpha(m)=n to be (p∘q)-coCartesian; its equivalence with the locally coCartesian condition defining Gamma_I here follows from Remark 4.2.2.22 (p. 519-520: composites with these edges preserve local coCartesianness), the dual of Higher Topos Theory (2009) Lemma 2.4.2.7, and HTT Proposition 2.4.1.3, since the algebra section carries these edges to coCartesian edges. The identification of each evaluation with the forgetful functor is also stated at the end of the proof of HA Proposition 4.2.3.4 (p. 528). Online source read; WANTED: archived Higher Algebra in literature/. No Stacks tag covers this coherent module model.

proof.text: Represent the given action by the cocartesian operadic fibration $r:\mathcal O\to L$ of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. Let $D=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ and use the explicit functors $\mathrm{Cut}$, $\mathrm{LCut}$ and the transformation $\gamma$ of [lem-coef-lm-prism-approximation]. Write $b=B\mathrm{Cut}:D\to\mathcal O$. Construct $X_B$ as follows: a $k$-simplex is a map $\sigma:\Delta^k\to D$ and a lift $h:\Delta^k\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal O$ of $\gamma(\sigma\times1)$ with top restriction $b\sigma$, all of whose vertex arrows over $\theta_n$ are inert. Operators restrict both maps. Thus $X_B$ is the full subcategory, on these inert arrows, of the degreewise pullback of the relative endpoint-$1$ corner map for $r$. This constructs the object and all its higher simplices; it is not a choice of data from an existence theorem.

source.place: Notation 4.2.2.17, fixed-algebra pullback (online, not archived; the argument is expanded here)

proof.text: The relative endpoint-$1$ corner map is a categorical fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], with the inclusion $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$; $r$ is a categorical fibration by its operadic definition. Pulling back its horn and equivalence lifting problems gives the same lifting properties for the unrestricted prism object over $D$. Restricting to the full subcategory in step 1 preserves them: an inner-horn filler has the same vertices, and an equivalence lift stays among inert vertex arrows. For the latter assertion, a square of arrows which is an equivalence in the arrow category has equivalences on both endpoints by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], so it preserves the homotopy-pullback test for an $r$-cocartesian arrow in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. Composition with these endpoint equivalences induces inverse maps up to the inverse-triangle homotopies, using [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], so the pullback test is unchanged. The base vertical arrow remains $\theta_n$. Consequently $q_B:X_B\to D$ is the required categorical fibration.

source.place: Remark 4.2.2.19; explicit endpoint-corner and full-subcategory argument (online, not archived; the argument is expanded here)

proof.text: For each $[n]$ construct the coherent last-colour projection. Put $K=(X_B)_{[n]}$ and let $a_n:K\to\mathcal O$ evaluate prisms at their bottom endpoint, over the constant base $w=(\langle n+1\rangle,\{n+1\})$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to $a_n$ and the constant transformation $w\to m$ given by the last-colour inert projection. Its target is a coherent functor $e_n:K\to\mathcal O_m=\mathcal M$. The hypothesis on all cocartesian lifts is supplied by the given left tensoring in [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. Thus $e_n$ is defined on coherent transformations and all higher simplices.

Apply [lem-coef-inert-projection-square-fibres] with $v$ a target vertex of $K$, $u$ a source vertex, $f=1_w$, and top edge the identity of $b([n])$. The projection $\theta_n$ discards only the module output, so the space of squares is the space of module-coordinate maps. The $K=\Delta^0$ mapping-space fibre formula in [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] identifies it with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(e_nu,e_nv)$; its projection is the map induced by $e_n$. Hence $e_n$ is fully faithful. For $x\in\mathcal M$, the Segal equivalence of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding] supplies the mixed tuple $(B,\ldots,B,x)$. An inert lift of $\theta_n$ has target equivalent to $b([n])$ in the pure Segal fibre; composing with this equivalence gives a vertex of $K$ mapping to $x$ up to equivalence. Thus $e_n$ is essentially surjective, and [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] supplies the fibre equivalence. When $n=0$ the pure fibre is terminal; the calculation still has just the module factor.

source.place: Remark 4.2.2.18; fixed-target square fibre and Segal essential surjectivity

proof.text: Fix $\beta=\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}:[n]\to[m]$. The block formula of [lem-coef-lm-prism-approximation] sends exactly the tail $(\alpha(m),n]$, followed by the module input, to the module output. For vertices $u,v$ over $[n],[m]$, an arrow over $\beta$ is a prism square with fixed top $b(\beta)$. Apply [lem-coef-inert-projection-square-fibres] to that square. Only the module output is discarded by $\theta_m$, leaving the operation space from the indicated tail and $e_nu$ to $e_mv$. Its ordered operation has cocartesian transport $t=B^{\otimes(n-\alpha(m))}\otimes e_nu$ by [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. The object case of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] identifies that operation space naturally with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(t,e_mv)$. These are equivalences on the full coherent parameter spaces, since both cited fibre formulas have that naturality. The exponent is nonnegative and an empty tail acts by the unit constraint.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2.20 and Remark 4.2.2.21; fixed-algebra operation calculation

proof.text: For each $\beta:[n]\to[m]$, pull $q_B$ back over its edge $\Delta^1\to D$. It is an inner fibration by step 2. Step 4 identifies both its endpoint fibres with $\mathcal M$, and step 5 represents its mixed mapping spaces at a source $x$ by $t=B^{\otimes(n-\alpha(m))}\otimes x$, coherently naturally in the target. Apply [lem-coef-mixed-mapping-cocartesian-recognition] with these fibre identifications. It gives a cocartesian edge over $\beta$ corresponding to the identity of $t$, and says that every other arrow over $\beta$ is locally cocartesian exactly when its represented module map $t\to y$ is an equivalence. Thus each edge pullback is a cocartesian fibration with precisely the asserted transport and local edge characterization.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2.20 and Remark 4.2.2.21; mapping-square recognition and explicit inverse test

proof.text: A coherent section of $q_B$, including transformations and higher simplices over $D$, is exactly a prism lift $F:D\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal O$ over $\gamma$, with fixed top $b$ and inert vertical edges: this is the degreewise exponential adjunction applied to step 1. If $\alpha:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$ is an interval inclusion ending at $n$, the algebra blocks each have one input and the module tail is empty. The algebra section $B$ carries the pure inert map to an inert arrow. Consequently the Segal projections make the mixed bottom edge inert exactly when its module comparison $x\to y$ is an equivalence: after inert transport the algebra comparisons are already equivalences, and the remaining comparison is the module map, by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. Step 6 identifies precisely that condition with local $q_B$-cocartesianness. Thus the bottom inert condition is exactly the condition defining $\Gamma_I(q_B)$. The marking classification of [lem-coef-lm-prism-approximation] exhausts the other marked edges: top ones are already inert because $B$ is an algebra, vertical ones are imposed by construction, and a marked cross edge factors through an inert vertical and an inert top edge. Their composite is inert by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], applied to $r$ and the corresponding prism triangle. Therefore $\Gamma_I(q_B)$ is exactly the category of lifts sending every $\gamma$-marked edge to an inert arrow and having fixed top $b$. This comparison checks the inert operadic condition directly; it assumes no global cocartesian condition on $q_B$.

source.place: Definition 4.2.2.10, Proposition 4.2.2.12, Corollary 4.2.2.16 and Remark 4.2.2.19; direct comparison of inert bottom edges (online, not archived; the argument is expanded here)

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction] to $\gamma:D\times\Delta^1\to L$, $r:\mathcal O\to L$, and to $\mathrm{Cut}:D\to A$, $r|_A$. The operadic and colour-equivalence hypotheses are supplied by [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding] and [lem-coef-lm-prism-approximation]. Restriction gives a commuting square of equivalences: operadic sections to marked prism lifts, and algebra sections to marked Cut lifts. For each vertical map apply [lem-coef-inert-marked-restriction-fibration], using the simplicial inclusions $A\subseteq L$ and $D\times\{1\}\subseteq D\times\Delta^1$, respectively. The markings are precisely the inert base arrows and their inverse images under $\gamma$, so the markings on the subobjects are inherited. The encoding makes $r$ categorical. Both vertical restrictions are therefore categorical fibrations on the full marked lift categories. Now [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] computes their strict fibres as pullbacks in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. Its test-category formula is invariant under the two horizontal equivalences, so the fibres at $B$ and $b=B\mathrm{Cut}$ are equivalent. The first is $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ by definition, the second is $\Gamma_I(q_B)$ by step 7. The comparison is restriction on all transformations and higher simplices and evaluates the original section at $m$ at $([0],0)$.

source.place: Corollary 4.2.2.16, via the two approximation equivalences and the existing categorical-fibration pullback theorem

proof.text: For $[n]$ use the opposite of the interval inclusion $[0]\hookrightarrow[n]$ selecting $n$. It belongs to $I$, and its transport is the identity on the module fibre by the empty-tail calculation. Every section in $\Gamma_I(q_B)$ consequently gives an equivalence $e_n(s([n]))\simeq e_0(s([0]))$. Evaluation of a coherent transformation of sections on this fixed base edge gives its naturality square, and evaluation of higher simplices gives all higher compatibilities. Under the restriction equivalence proved in step 8, evaluation at $([0],0)$ is the value of the operadic section at $m$, which is $U$ by [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. The componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes this a coherent natural equivalence. Composing gives the requested natural equivalence between every evaluation and $U$. At $n=0$ it is the identity. All preceding constructions used only the specified operadic tensoring, its mapping spaces and categorical-fibration lifting; no existence or preservation of colimits, limits or presentability was invoked.

source.place: End of proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed p. 528; terminal-vertex evaluation comparison (online, not archived; the argument is expanded here)

proof_origin.place: Agent expansion of HA Notation 4.2.2.17, Remarks 4.2.2.18-21 and Corollary 4.2.2.16: explicit inert-prism construction and mapping-space calculation, with a general approximation theorem and combinatorial Cut/prism approximation as separate statement-only dependencies. Read online; source not archived in literature/.
